text:
chris - support: Customer (Acme Corp) reporting lots of 5xx / auth failures and 200s with 600ms+ RTT. They insist requests should target eu-west but logs show us-east served. Escalating to infra/sre.

maria - support: Can you paste an example request id / curl + headers they used?

chris - support: Provided by customer:
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Host: api.redwood.ai' -H 'X-Region-Hint: eu-west' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response headers they got: `x-active-region: us-east` and `x-gateway-route: svc-us-east-v2`

acme-integration-bot: [automated] request_id=acme-8442 path=/v1/generate latency_ms=620 upstream=svc-us-east-v2 status=200 auth_time=0.85s

kevin - infra: Thanks. I pulled gateway logs for that request_id — header arrives intact on edge, but an L7 rewrite step normalizes headers and afterwards I see `x-region-hint` dropped and `x-region` being set by the route selection. Looks like our route matcher fell back to a region affinity route because header lookup failed.

samira - eng-sre: Did we deploy the new L7 header normalization change yesterday? deploy-bot tag?

deploy-bot: deploy finished: gateway/v2 2026-02-25T18:03:12Z by @kevin — change: header-normalization: enabled; header-whitelist: reduced

kevin - infra: Yep — that change tightened the header whitelist to prevent arbitrary client headers being used for routing. I suspect the whitelist inadvertently excluded `X-Region-Hint` (case-normalized) and a fallback rule uses a substring match on `x-region` which then picks us-east.

maria - support: Customer also seeing 401 occasionally. Could be auth backend in eu-west timing out due to cross-region traffic.

kevin - infra: Repro steps from my laptop:
```
# send hint, inspect gateway matched route header
curl -v -H 'X-Region-Hint: eu-west' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
# then tail gateway logs grep request_id=<id>
```
I can reproduce header being dropped when header-normalization policy removes unknown headers. Route matcher then matches route with region affinity header `x-region: us-east` and rewrites downstream.

samira - eng-sre: OK this feels like a config regression: header whitelist too strict + a fallback substring matcher for `x-region` that's overbroad. Short-term mitigation: add `x-region-hint` to whitelist and add a rewrite to copy it into `x-region` when present. I'll prepare a config patch and do a safe rollout.

maria - support: Can we give Acme a temporary workaround while you patch?

chris - support: They can set `?region=eu-west` query param — that bypasses L7 header match and picks the right backend for now. I shared that with them.

kevin - infra: I prepared the whitelist change and a rewrite rule. Patch: add `x-region-hint` to allowed list and a `preserve_and_copy` rewrite to set `x-region` from `x-region-hint` if present. Will roll to canary first.

samira - eng-sre: Rolling canary now to 10% nodes (gateway/canary). Monitoring latency and auth errors.

deploy-bot: rollout started: gateway-config 2026-02-26T02:14:03Z target=canary(10%) by @samira

kevin - infra: Canary logs show requests with `X-Region-Hint: eu-west` now complete with `x-active-region: eu-west` and RTTs back to ~80ms for EU customers. Auth timing improved.

maria - support: Shared interim fix and ETA with Acme. They're patching their integration to keep `X-Region-Hint` in capitalized form for now. :thumbsup:

samira - eng-sre: Canary looks stable for 30m. Promoting to 100% now.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: gateway-config 2026-02-26T02:48:21Z status=success

samira - eng-sre: Followup actions: 1) revert the overly aggressive header-whitelist reduction in next minor release (tracked), 2) add unit tests for header-preservation and route matching, 3) audit other matchers for substring collisions. I'll open the JIRA.

kevin - infra: Filed INFRA-7123 with the config diff and repro steps. Putting a short postmortem note into ops channel after lunch.

chris - support: Acme confirmed resolved. They saw P95 drop and no more auth breaks. Thanks team.

maria - support: Closing the customer escalation but keeping monitoring for 24h.

chris - support: Marking this thread for postmortem if any regression surfaces. :white_check_mark:
